decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 3.5% to 3.75%. The vote was 8-4. Dissenting: Stephen I. Miran, Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, Lorie K. Logan.

tone_quotes.quote: Inflation is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices.

The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments.
Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 20.97% APR costs about $87.38 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.42% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.3% would rise by about $11.75 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.3%, and employers added an average of 73k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.3% over the past year (March 2026); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +8 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.04%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.27% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 94%, cut 6%, hike 0%.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.
